witness_description: On the labeled vertex set {v_1,v_2}, take G with E(G)=∅. It is finite, undirected, simple, and triangle-free. Both degrees are 0; the construction gives V(H)=∅ and E(H)=∅, hence V(B(H))=∅, while C_1=C_2=∅.
refutation_explanation: The claim requires each C_i to be a vertex C_H(e) of B(H) and requires the C_i to be pairwise distinct. Here H has no edges, so B(H) has no vertices at all; neither empty C_i is a vertex of B(H), and C_1=C_2. Thus phi cannot be a bijection or an isomorphism.
search_space: All 2 finite undirected simple graphs on the fixed labeled vertex set {v_1,v_2}, enumerated by the two masks for the sole possible edge {v_1,v_2}; both graphs are triangle-free, and the full two-mask space was swept in increasing mask order.
